title: Seed Dormancy and Germination Response Protocol
author: Corrine Duncan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6cehate

steps.title: Test Seed Viability
steps.instruction: Determine seed viability using tetrazolium chloride (TZ) staining and water germination tests.

substeps.instruction: Place seeds in a petri dish and soak with a 1% solution of 2,3,5-triphenyl tetrazolium chloride (TZ).
Incubate seeds under diurnal temperatures for at least 48 hours.
Extract seeds and perform longitudinal dissections under a microscope.
Record seeds that stain bright red or pink as viable, and seeds that remain unstained or partially stained as non-viable.
Verify TZ results by germinating seeds on filter paper moistened with distilled water at diurnal temperatures (for non-dormant seeds).

steps.title: Test Seed Longevity
steps.instruction: Assess viability loss over time by storing seeds under controlled conditions.

substeps.instruction: Perform initial viability test using the TZ method.
Remove excess organic matter from the seed batch.
Store seeds in paper bags under constant dark, air-conditioned temperatures (10-20°C), and low humidity (<50%).
Monitor and record temperature and humidity frequently.
Extract 100 seeds at 0, 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months and test for viability using the TZ method.

steps.title: Perform Imbibition Tests
steps.instruction: Measure seed weight increase over time under different temperature regimes.

substeps.instruction: Weigh four replicates of 25 seeds while dry.
Place seeds on moist filter paper and incubate under a 12 hr light/dark schedule at three diurnal temperatures: 30/20°C, 25/15°C, and 17/7°C.
After 5 minutes on moist filter paper, remove seeds, pat dry with a paper towel to remove surface moisture, and re-weigh.
Re-weigh seeds at 10 min, 30 min, and at 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, 168, and 192+ hours.

steps.title: Classify Dormancy and Germination Responses
steps.instruction: Determine dormancy types based on germination response to temperature and gibberellic acid (GA3).

substeps.instruction: Surface sterilize seeds by soaking in 1% sodium hypochlorite for one minute, then rinse for 40 seconds with double distilled water.
Place four replicates of 25 seeds per species in 90-mm diameter petri dishes on filter paper moistened with distilled water.
Incubate at a 12/12-hr light/dark regime at daily alternating temperatures of 30/20°C, 25/15°C, and 17/7°C.
To test GA3 effects, incubate seeds at 30/20°C using filter paper moistened with a 350 ppm GA3 solution.
Record germination (radicle emerged to at least half of seed size) daily for 30 days, or until germination ceases for four consecutive readings across all treatments.

Classify as non-dormant if seeds germinate without pre-treatment; physiologically dormant if they imbibe water and respond to GA3 but do not germinate within 30 days; physically dormant if they do not imbibe water or germinate.

steps.title: Alleviate Physiological Dormancy
steps.instruction: Apply treatments to break physiological dormancy, specifically for Atriplex.

substeps.instruction: Apply after-ripening by storing seeds for one year under constant dark and air-conditioned temperatures (as per longevity storage conditions).
Expose after-ripened seeds to the germination treatments described in the classification step.
Alternatively, apply the move-along method or soak seeds in boiling water and 90% H2SO4.
